S14.item: NZ-03 insert shoulder gasket (mica / vermiculite 1 mm)

hot_layer.atmosphere: N2O/ABS exhaust: CO, H2, H2O, CO2, N2; free O2 up to 12 % at O/F 8-11.6 (§4.6)
hot_layer.bearing_MPa: 10.6 at BN 63.1 bar; strength >= 2x at temperature
hot_layer.k_through_W_mK: <= ~1 (keeps the lip at or below the present 250 C in-burn)
hot_layer.compatibility: no SiO2 in contact with graphite above ~1400-1500 C (SiO2 + 3C -> SiC + 2CO, as recalled, TO-VERIFY)

seal_layer.T_service: in-burn face temperature from the FE re-run + 100 K; today 250.6 C in-burn, 653.5 C soak at the lip (FE)
seal_layer.tightness: gas-tight at MEOP 45 bar; seated by the insert at BN 63.1 bar
seal_layer.life: replaced at every insert change (one per flight)

candidates.hot_layer: carbon-phenolic flange 2.0 mm, integral with NZ-02 (top-hat sleeve) or a separate washer
candidates.seal: 0.5 mm flexible graphite ring (oxidation-inhibited grade) or the present 1 mm mica/vermiculite ring at the lip face
candidates.why: same ablative family as NZ-02; carbon char is compatible with graphite; low virgin k; tolerates the 1593 C hot face by charring
candidates.risks: char depth and shrinkage (preload is pressure-energised); pyrolysis gas into the annulus (vents to the chamber via the grooves)
candidates.tags: LITERATURE as recalled, TO-VERIFY (char rate, k, char strength)

candidates.hot_layer: dense fully stabilised zirconia washer 1.5-2.0 mm, lapped faces
candidates.seal: 0.5 mm flexible graphite ring at the lip face
candidates.why: survives > 2000 C, inert in oxidising gas, strong in compression
candidates.risks: thermal-shock cracking (acceptable only while confined and in compression); k ~2-2.5 W/mK raises the seal-face and lip temperature: FE to show

candidates.seal: metal C-ring (Inconel 718 / X-750, silver plated) in a lip groove
candidates.risks: groove in a 6 mm lip; separate bearing path; rated ~700 C class as recalled

items: flexible graphite on the hot face (oxidises in O2-bearing gas at 1600 C)
silica- or glass-bearing layers against graphite above ~1500 C
alumina-silica or alumina fibre paper as the bearing layer (crushes far below 10.6 MPa, as recalled)

side_finding.NZ02: NZ-02 peaks at 1551 C (r 22, soak). A glass-phenolic sleeve would melt its glass (E-glass softens far below that, as recalled); silica-phenolic reacts with the graphite above ~1500 C. Carbon-phenolic is the conventional backing for graphite inserts. Mechanical to confirm the NZ-02 material in the same FE re-run.

verification: Mechanical FE re-run with the two-layer stack and contact conductances (hot-layer peak, seal-face peak in-burn and soak, lip peak)
T1: thermocouple well in the lip at r 21 (planned) plus one at the lip bore edge
pressure-decay leak check of the assembled joint with N2 at 67.5 bar before and after every firing (criterion TO-DEFINE with Mechanical)
post-test: section the hot layer (char depth or cracks), inspect the lip bore and the spigot OD for leak tracks, measure stack height loss
